source.title: Evidence for feature-specific error correction in LLMs
source.citation: Francisco Ferreira da Silva et al., 2026
source.authors: Francisco Ferreira da Silva; S. Heimersheim

page_placements.theme: Feature-specific error correction and anisotropic perturbation responses

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests feature-specific perturbation-response geometry as evidence for error correction in superposition, using a new measure rather than the original toy-model geometry method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports measured superellipse exponents, rotation sweeps, and perturbation-layer/metric/threshold ablations. Prompt examples of steering and values used to set thresholds are not separate findings here. The ablation figure reports individual settings graphically; the text states that the results hold across all of them.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether models are more sensitive to candidate feature directions than to mixtures of them (superellipse exponent p). The authors read this as evidence of error correction for computation in superposition. That is a different construct from every listed version. It does not measure overlap or near-orthogonality of stored features, a sparsity transition, neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation, spread across neurons, or SAE completeness, stability or canonicity. It does not compare 1-D with multi-dimensional features. Its response model assumes superposition: it relies on the near-orthogonal packing of features (Elhage et al.) so the two-direction fit approximation holds. Its p=2 argument concerns more directions than dimensions, but only pairs of directions are ever tested. The authors also call p>2 necessary but not sufficient for a direction to be a feature. The SAE row (r3) shows SAE decoder directions are privileged, but that does not test whether SAEs recover the model's sparse features (V4) or are its canonical units (V5). The reader's 'tests'/T2 conflicts with its own finding that every version is not_tested. Results belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that contrastive, MELBO and top-activating SAE directions are privileged over their mixtures (p≈2.2–2.3 versus ≈2 for controls). They present this as the first empirical evidence of feature-specific error correction and as evidence favouring superposition and computation in superposition in LLMs. They treat the measured p as likely a lower bound. They caveat that p>2 is necessary but not sufficient for a direction to be a feature, and that plateaus might reflect learned robustness or on-manifold correction instead.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses residual-stream perturbations and fits superellipse exponents to downstream response boundaries; it does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports robustness across perturbation and measurement layers, response metric, threshold, perturbation method, activation source, token position, and model; individual ablation values are figure-only.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2-9B, contrastive, MELBO and SAE-decoder directions give mean p of 2.21–2.42, above 2. PCA, random-difference and random controls give ~2.03–2.05. p falls toward 2 as contrastive directions are rotated toward random. Contrastive p>2 holds across six models and setup ablations (means 2.24–2.63).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM residual-stream perturbation responses privilege candidate feature directions over their mixtures, consistent with feature-specific error correction for computation in superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: In a two-layer denoising network computing in superposition, true feature directions give p of 3–3.4, increasing with feature-to-neuron ratio. p declines to 2 under rotation, and ~0.8 cosine alignment gives p of 2.3–2.6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Error-correcting toy networks in superposition privilege true feature directions over mixtures, and the perturbation exponent detects this.

record.problems: The LLM experiments lack ground-truth feature directions, so candidate directions may be imperfect; the paper itself says p > 2 is necessary but not sufficient for a direction to be a feature. The authors note that plateaus may reflect learned robustness or a lower-dimensional activation manifold rather than error correction. Toy-model results are from a two-layer network with binary features and tanh3 activation, and the paper says not to place much weight on its specific values. Several ablation values are presented only graphically.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each of the 40 rotated pairs or 80 toy-model direction pairs: the text reports their aggregate sweep results. No separate rows for individual ablation dots beyond the listed distinct settings; plotted values are not given numerically in the text.

untested.parts: Overlap and near-orthogonality of stored features, the sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry are not measured. The toy denoising network is used only to validate the perturbation method.
No neuron polysemanticity or allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions is measured.
Polysemanticity and its causes are not studied.
There is no measure of features spread across neurons, nor of whether SAEs recover sparse features. SAE decoder directions are only probed for perturbation sensitivity relative to mixtures (r3).
SAE completeness, stability and canonicity are not tested. Only one SAE (Gemma Scope 16k, layer 2) and 33 top-active latents are used.
1-D directions are assumed. Multi-dimensional features are not compared; the manifold alternative is raised only in the discussion.

missing.what: Aggregate ablation range for contrastive directions: means [2.24, 2.63], medians [2.11, 2.50] across all settings and models.
Toy-model misalignment result: ~0.8 cosine alignment reduces p from 3–3.4 to 2.3–2.6.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's record was internally inconsistent: relation 'tests' with every version not_tested. It is reclassified as assumes/T4, because the method's two-direction approximation relies on near-orthogonal superposed features. The claim of evidence for superposition is indirect and rests on a theoretical argument (p=2 cannot privilege more than d_model directions), not on any measurement of more-features-than-dimensions. If the phenomenon file later adds a version about computation in superposition or error correction, these rows would bear on it. SAE results cover Gemma-2-9B only.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure feature-storage overlap, near-orthogonality, a sparsity-dependent transition, or the regular geometry specified in this version.
No neuron polysemanticity or allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions is measured.
The study does not test polysemanticity or alternative causes of it.
The study measures responses along candidate SAE decoder directions, but does not test whether SAE dictionaries recover sparse features or whether LLM features spread across neurons.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study uses candidate directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: two-layer denoising network (Vaintrob, 2026)
rows.operation_detail: Fit superellipse exponent for perturbations along pairs of true inactive feature directions, then rotate perturbations away from those directions.

relation.reason: Superposition motivates the error-correction prediction and is built into the toy model. The empirical findings are interpreted as consistent with superposition, without directly measuring the listed versions.

tranche.reason: The toy model uses known superposition to validate a directional-privileging measurement. The LLM experiments measure feature-specific sensitivity, a related construct that does not directly test any listed version.

source_check.notes: All listed numerical results are supported. Rotation is specifically toward random directions; r9 and r10 are illustrative method-validation examples, not independent evidence for a catalog version.
